title: Mask of Tutankhamun
medium: Gold, lapis lazuli, carnelian, quartz, obsidian, turquoise, faience, and colored glass
dimensions: 54 cm tall, approximately 10.23 kg of solid gold
short_description: The golden funerary mask of the boy-king Tutankhamun, made to cover his mummified face.
long_description: The Mask of Tutankhamun is a funerary mask discovered in 1925 by Howard Carter inside the tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings. The mask was placed directly over the face of the king's mummified body. It is made of two sheets of solid gold hammered together and inlaid with semi-precious stones and colored glass.
historical_context: Tutankhamun became pharaoh as a child around 1332 BCE and died at about 18 or 19. His tomb is one of the only Egyptian royal tombs found largely intact. The mask reflects ancient Egyptian beliefs about the afterlife.
anecdote: When Howard Carter first lifted the heavy lid of Tutankhamun's innermost coffin to reveal the mask, he later wrote that the gold was so reflective it seemed as if they gazed upon the face of a god.
